newsitem.title: USA: US corporate mart ends busy week on a high note.
newsitem.headline: US corporate mart ends busy week on a high note.

text.p: The U.S. corporate bond market ended a busy week on a high note as spreads held firm in the face of over $6 billion in new issuance, traders said.
Prices among investment-grade and high-yield bonds were unchanged to slightly higher at the end of trading on Friday, traders said.

In the investment grade market, traders said prices in the bank sector rallied late on Friday. Spreads on most bank bonds closed several basis points tighter, after widening three to four basis points in the morning, they said.
The onslaught of more than 15 offerings of a new type of preferred stock by banks throughout the week had earlier battered prices on outstanding bank debt.
By Friday afternoon, one trader said, "People started realizing that these levels were getting out of hand, and that caused spreads to tighten back up."
The high-yield market on Friday was dominated by trading of several new issues which priced throughout the day.
After hitting the market, Newport News Shipbuilding senior notes were bid up to 101 3/4 and its senior subordinated notes were bid up to 102, traders said.

One trader from a smaller junk broker/dealer firm explained, "Firms that are not involved in the new-issue market are looking to trade bonds to stay in the game. We've got to show our customers that we're staying involved."
After digesting over $1 billion in new high-yield bonds this week, junk players were eagerly anticipating a $475 million deal by Allied Waste North America which is scheduled to price next Monday.
The transaction, lead managed by Goldman Sachs & Co, is about six times oversubscribed, market sources say.
Allied Waste will use the proceeds from the 144a private placement offering to finance its acquisition of the solid waste division of Laidaw Inc.
The transaction has been well-received by investors, increasing demand for the new paper, analysts said.
Additionally, junk players are often draw to large deals, which because of their liquidity, are easily tradable.
